newsitem.title: USA: Fumes force closing of Houston airport terminal.
newsitem.headline: Fumes force closing of Houston airport terminal.

text.p: Fumes from a canister filled with an experimental pesticide sent three people to the hospital and forced officials to shut the international terminal at Houston Intercontinental Airport Thursday, an airport spokesman said.
U.S. Customs Service agents seized the canister from an international passenger who arrived in Houston on a KLM Royal Dutch Airlines flight from Amsterdam, airport spokesman Richard Fernandez said.

"Customs kept the package for about four hours when it began emitting fumes," he said. Three people complaining of dizziness and nausea were hospitalized for observation in the incident, which shut the international terminal for more than three hours.

A hazardous materials team determined that fumes from the pesticide, which was brought from India, were not toxic. Airport officials were uncertain whether it had been carried on board or checked by the passenger in Amsterdam.

The passenger, who was not identified, was allowed to continue with his trip. "Charges could be brought. It's up to the (U.S. Federal Aviation Administration) and other officials," Fernandez said. "It appears to be an unintentional thing."
Passengers on several international flights through Houston were delayed until the terminal was aired out and reopened shortly before 11 p.m. EDT (0200 GMT Friday), he said.
